Consult Summary:
- 32-year-old female nurse with one-week history of fever, night sweats, myalgia, nausea and malaise after recent travel to Vietnam (returned 4 weeks ago); plan for in-person examination and blood tests including malaria films; advised not to work until assessment complete.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Fever for approximately 7 days: patient reports being "really hot and sweaty all the time."
  - Associated symptoms: generalized myalgia/aching, persistent nausea with reduced oral intake, night sweats, intermittent chills (periods of feeling hot and cold without clear pattern), marked fatigue and malaise.
- Timeline/progression:
  - Symptoms began ~7 days ago and have persisted without resolution despite OTC antipyretics.
  - Returned from travel to Vietnam 4 weeks prior to presentation.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Over-the-counter paracetamol and ibuprofen taken at recommended doses daily; described as taking "the edge off" but not resolving symptoms.
  - No other specific relieving or exacerbating factors reported.
- Associated symptoms / systems review:
  - Respiratory: denies cough, cold, sore throat.
  - ENT: denies ear pain.
  - Gastrointestinal: nausea present; denies diarrhea.
  - Neurologic: baseline headaches related to screen use/migraines for years; no new or severe headache or neck stiffness.
  - Genitourinary: denies dysuria, frequency, or urinary symptoms.
  - Dermatologic / Musculoskeletal: denies rash; no swollen or tender peripheral joints; chronic back pain present.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No cough, sore throat, ear pain, diarrhea, neck stiffness, new severe headache, rash, joint swelling, or urinary symptoms documented.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic low back pain; currently under treatment by physiotherapist (diagnosed as posture-related, exercises for strengthening).
- No other chronic medical conditions reported.
- Medications:
  - Seroxat (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Occasional/regular use of paracetamol and ibuprofen for current symptoms (dose/route/frequency: "recommended dose" not documented).
- Allergies:
  - Pollen (hay fever). No drug allergies reported.

Social History:
- Occupation: nurse (healthcare worker); up to date with vaccinations including Hepatitis B per patient.
- Tobacco: non-smoker.
- Alcohol: moderate intake (no quantities specified).
- Exercise: moderate physical exercise a few times per week.
- Travel: recent travel to Vietnam; visited cities and rural/countryside/farmland, undertook trekking and cycling; returned 4 weeks ago.
- No other social factors (housing, occupational exposures beyond nursing) documented.

Family History:
- Father deceased from myocardial infarction (approximate age at death 68).

Physical Examination:
- No vital signs or physical examination findings documented in the transcript.

Investigations:
- Planned/ordered (no results available):
  - Thick and thin blood films for malaria.
  - Inflammatory markers and other blood tests (specific panels not fully specified).
- No imaging or laboratory results documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute febrile illness with systemic features (fever, night sweats, myalgia, nausea, fatigue)
  - Assessment: Febrile illness of unclear focus; no respiratory, ENT, urinary, or GI source identified on history.
  - Plan:
    - Arrange in-person clinic assessment/examination by GP in central London to identify focus of infection and determine urgency of testing.
    - Obtain blood tests including inflammatory markers.
    - Advise patient not to attend work until cause is investigated and cleared.
- Issue 2: Recent travel to Vietnam with rural exposure — concern for malaria and other travel-related infections
  - Assessment: Travel-associated febrile illness; malaria must be excluded given rural exposure and recent travel.
  - Plan:
    - Request thick and thin blood films to evaluate for malaria after clinical assessment.
    - Documented plan to include malaria films and relevant travel-related tests in the clinic note for use if patient presents to local A&E.
    - Urgency of malaria testing to be determined based on examination findings; clinician to prioritize accordingly.
- Issue 3: Chronic low back pain
  - Assessment: Chronic, posture-related back pain currently managed with physiotherapy.
  - Plan:
    - No acute change reported; continue physiotherapy program as advised by treating physiotherapist.
- General plan items:
  - Administrative: clinician will ask admin team to book patient into clinic; patient instructed to phone the number left in consultation notes to be scheduled and to bring clinic note to A&E if attending there instead.
  - If unable to attend central clinic, patient may present to local A&E with clinician's note to expedite testing.
  - Symptomatic care: patient has been using paracetamol/ibuprofen as needed; continue as appropriate (no new prescriptions documented).

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No vital signs documented (e.g., temperature, heart rate, blood pressure, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation).
  - No physical examination findings recorded.
  - No laboratory or imaging results available.
  - Medication dose/route/frequency not documented for Seroxat and OTC analgesics.
  - No explicit documentation of malaria prophylaxis medication name, dose, duration, or adherence (patient uncertain).
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Malaria prophylaxis details conflict/uncertain: patient cannot recall exact medication; stated it was "daily" and also implied she took "another one on top of the first one" — specifics unclear (conflict/uncertainty noted).
- Transcript quality:
  - Audio/dialogue largely intelligible; occasional missed phrases and brief interruptions but overall adequate to extract clinical information.
